=============================================================================
4. OPEN-SOURCE PRODUCT: GRIDWRIGHT (apsw-gridwright)
=============================================================================
Gridwright is a React data grid published on npm under the MIT licence, built on a headless,
framework-agnostic engine. Latest release: 0.22.1 (2026-10-24).

- One pipeline for local and remote data: a data source declares which parts of the query it
  resolved (sort, filter, search, paginate) and the grid applies the rest in memory. Swapping
  `data` for `dataSource` is a one-line change; columns and add-ons stay the same.
- Real table semantics: a <table> with role="grid", aria-sort on the header, one live region, and
  an opt-in wcag() add-on for WCAG 2.2 AA sizing and colours.
- Every feature is an add-on: search, column filters, tree data, grouping with aggregates, export
  (CSV, Excel, Markdown, print, PDF), row and column virtualization (up to ten million rows),
  column layout, inline editing, row detail, cell navigation, responsive layout, URL sync, density,
  loading indicators, row actions.
- Zero runtime dependencies, about 17 kB gzipped for the component, React 18 and 19, TypeScript,
  ESM and CommonJS, translations for en, de, es, fr and pl. Companion package apsw-gridwright-mui
  takes colours, type and dark mode from an MUI theme.
- Never invents a total: when an API sends no count, the grid reports "of many".
- Not included: pivot tables, built-in charts, range selection.
- Licensing: the grid and every add-on are free (MIT). A Pro tier (additional add-ons, priority
  support, migration help) is planned and not priced yet.
- Links: https://www.npmjs.com/package/apsw-gridwright | https://github.com/yaotzin1/apsw-gridwright |
  https://yaotzin1.github.io/apsw-gridwright/examples/playground/index.html

Delivery assurance (https://apsw.pl/#assurance): Gridwright is built by one architect with the
Indaba engine and coding agents under a single workflow.ai.yml that outranks every other
instruction. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md and skill pointers are generated from it; each rule is
marked enforced (a hook, CI job, lint rule or test fails) or guidance; every commit declares its
track (feature, fix, chore, release) and the trailer is checked against the diff; verification
covers smoke tests of the built package, a packaging audit and a security audit. The repository
carries over 1,300 automated tests. APSW brings the same setup to client teams.
